name: Pavitr Prabhakar
summary: Marvel's Mumbai-set Spider-Man: a village boy who gains spider powers from a yogi. He debuted in the Spider-Man: India miniseries (2004, cover-dated January 2005) and later swung into the Spider-Verse films.
origin: Pavitr is a shy village teenager who moves to Mumbai with his Auntie Maya and Uncle Bhim on a partial scholarship and is teased for his rural background. While fleeing bullies he meets a yogi who grants him spider-like abilities. When Uncle Bhim is fatally injured, Pavitr vows to protect others. He faces crime lord Nalin Oberoi, who is possessed by a demon through an amulet. The setting is Earth-50101 in Marvel's multiverse.
creators: Debdatta Das (credited co-creator in some listings)
powers: Superhuman strength, speed, agility and reflexes

storyline.title: A village boy in Mumbai
storyline.beat: Spider-Man: India retells the Spider-Man origin in Mumbai, with a yogi granting powers and a demon-possessed crime lord named Nalin Oberoi as the main enemy.

storyline.title: Spider-Verse
storyline.beat: Pavitr joins the great gathering of Spider-people across realities, is saved from a villain named Karn and is recruited by the Superior Spider-Man.

storyline.title: Arachnia and the Web Warriors
storyline.beat: During Secret Wars he lives in the domain of Arachnia beside Spider-Gwen, Spider-Ham, Noir, Spider-UK and Anya Corazon; the team is later named the Web Warriors.

storyline.title: Watching Earth-3145
storyline.beat: He helps monitor a world where the Inheritors have grown weak from hunger, alongside Spider-Girl, Spider-Punk, Spider-UK and Master Weaver.

storyline.title: Mumbattan on the big screen
storyline.beat: Across the Spider-Verse introduces Mumbattan, voiced by Karan Soni in English, with Pavitr part of the Spider Society and dating Gayatri.

gossip.text: Pavitr first appeared in the Spider-Man: India miniseries, dated 2004 in India or January 2005 elsewhere, long before his 2023 Hollywood animated film.
Deepak Chopra, better known for self-help books, chaired the company that helped launch the Indian Spider-Man, and Shekhar Kapur was its chief creative officer.
Khaleej Times, citing Harper's Bazaar, says Satyajit Ray once showed Stan Lee sketches for an Indian Spider-Man. The tale is widely repeated, but no first-hand account backs it.
The name Pavitr Prabhakar was written as a phonetic twist on Peter Parker.
Pavitr was bullied in the comic for his village roots and for wearing a dhoti, and an old press report even had him bouncing off Mumbai rickshaws.

quiz.q: Who gives Pavitr Prabhakar his powers in the original comic?
quiz.why: A yogi grants Pavitr spider powers while he is running from bullies.

quiz.q: What is the film nickname of Pavitr's home world?
Which cricketer voiced Pavitr in the Hindi and Punjabi film dubs?
quiz.why: Shubman Gill was announced for the Hindi and Punjabi dubs in May 2023.

quiz.q: Pavitr's comic counterpart of Mary Jane is called what?
quiz.why: Meera Jain is the Indian counterpart of Mary Jane Watson.

quiz.q: Which Indian martial art inspires Pavitr's fighting style in Across the Spider-Verse?
quiz.why: Pavitr's film fighting style draws on kalaripayattu.

theme.tagline: Swinging past rickshaws, one rooftop at a time.

timeline.title: Spider-Man: India launches
timeline.note: Gotham Entertainment Group publishes the four-issue Mumbai-set miniseries with Marvel; sources date issue #1 to 2004 in India or to January 2005.

timeline.title: US edition
timeline.note: The series is published in the United States and later collected as a trade paperback.

timeline.title: Joins Spider-Verse
timeline.note: Pavitr is recruited by the Superior Spider-Man, Doctor Octopus's mind in Peter Parker's body, during the multiverse-wide event.

timeline.title: Web Warriors form
timeline.note: Secret Wars gathers him with Spider-Gwen, Spider-Ham, Noir, Spider-UK and Anya Corazon.

timeline.title: Spider-Geddon
timeline.note: He watches Earth-3145 as part of a team of Spider-people monitoring the Inheritors.

timeline.title: Across the Spider-Verse
timeline.note: Karan Soni voices him in English and Shubman Gill in Hindi and Punjabi; Miles saves Inspector Singh in Mumbattan.

facts.text: Reports in 2004 said the Green Goblin would be a reincarnated rakshasa; in the finished comic the Goblin role goes to Nalin Oberoi, a crime lord possessed by a demon through an amulet.
A yogi grants Pavitr his spider powers while bullies chase him, replacing the radioactive spider of the original story with a mystical gift.
A 2004 press report described the new hero as bouncing off Mumbai rickshaws while wearing a dhoti, a loose traditional garment, over his costume.
The comic's Peter Parker cast is renamed: Mary Jane becomes Meera Jain, Aunt May is Auntie Maya, Uncle Ben is Uncle Bhim, and Harry Osborn becomes Hari Oberoi.
The film's artists emptied Manhattan's East River to carve a chasm, then stacked Mumbattan in levels and printed its look like old Indian comics with visible paper texture.
Pavitr's film suit was designed by artist Naveen Selvanathan, who mixed the 1964 Spider-Man costume with Theyyam and Yakshagana dance, temple architecture and henna patterns.

Co-director Joaquim Dos Santos says many of the film's artists grew up in India reading Indrajal Comics, and Phil Lord says the team set out to recreate how those comics were printed, so viewers can feel the grain of the paper.
Cricketer Shubman Gill voiced Pavitr in the Hindi and Punjabi dubs of Across the Spider-Verse, announced in May 2023.
Pavitr's fighting style in Across the Spider-Verse is inspired by kalaripayattu, an Indian martial art.
Slashfilm notes that, unlike most Spider-Men, the film's Pavitr has not yet suffered an origin-story tragedy, because he is still early in his hero career.

Miguel O'Hara says each Spider-Person has fixed canon events, such as the death of a police captain. Miles breaks the rule in Mumbattan by saving Inspector Singh, Gayatri's father, and Pavitr's world starts to collapse.
Pavitr Prabhakar is set to return in the sequel Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse, which Wikipedia lists for 2027.
Sharad Devarajan told the BBC that in 2004 Indians had seen pictures of Spider-Man but did not know his story or have comics about him, so the team reimagined him for India.
Khaleej Times says Pavitr's film outfit adds a dhoti and gold cuffs to the classic red-and-blue Spider-Man suit.
In the film Pavitr is a member of Miguel O'Hara's Spider-Society, is friends with Spider-Punk and Spider-Woman, and his wrist bands work as web-shooters.
You can play Pavitr in games: he is unlockable in Spider-Man Unlimited and Marvel Strike Force, and playable in Marvel Contest of Champions.

In the Spider-Verse comics Pavitr mistakes the villain Karn for a demon and is saved by the Superior Spider-Man, who is Doctor Octopus's mind in Peter Parker's body, then recruited into his army of Spiders.
The Web Warriors name for the team of six Spiders formed in Secret Wars was coined by Peter Parker, taken from the Ultimate Spider-Man TV series.
io9 ranked Pavitr fourteenth among the greatest alternate Spider-Men, calling him the best foreign Spider-Man Marvel has tried, while Screen Rant put him tenth.
The film crew nicknamed Earth-50101 'Mumbattan' after Mumbai and Manhattan, because the world is based on Gotham Entertainment's Spider-Man: India comic series.

kidSummary: Pavitr Prabhakar is India's Spider-Man. A village boy in Mumbai gets spider powers from a yogi in the comics, and later swings through Mumbattan in the Spider-Verse films.
